characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EBSD system on a field emission gun SEM (FEI Quanta 650, Thermo Fisher Scientific); 20 kV; step size 0.5 μm; specimens mechanically ground and electro-polished in 7% Nital at room temperature; Channel 5 post-processing software; grain size by linear intercept with 15° boundary misorientation definition.
characterization_methods.key_findings: For Al-8 only FCC austenite is present (no BCC ferrite); equiaxed austenite grains densely intersected by straight parallel twin boundaries; average austenite grain size ~28.3 μm, twin boundary fraction f_Tw = 50.3%.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Operating voltage 20 kV, step size 0.5 μm
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine phase distribution, grain size and twin boundary fraction as a function of alloying content.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: TEM (Tecnai G2 F20 S-TWIN, Thermo Fisher Scientific) at 200 kV; thin foils twin-jet electro-polished in 10% perchloric acid + 90% ethanol at 20 V and −20 °C.
characterization_methods.key_findings: No κ-carbides were observed in the Fe30Mn(x)Al1C steel with 8% Al (Fig. 5(e)); bright-field image and inset SAED show only γ reflections ((000), (020)γ, (200)γ) with no κ spots.
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine κ-carbide precipitation in the solution-treated samples.
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (bright-field imaging with SAED; dark-field imaging of κ phase)

characterization_methods.key_findings: Al-8: UTS 826 ± 2 MPa, YS 548 ± 4 MPa, uniform elongation 74 ± 1.1%, total elongation 74.0 ± 1%.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Ambient temperature, initial strain rate 1.1 × 10^-3 s^-1; gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm
characterization_methods.purpose: Obtain engineering stress-strain response and corresponding strain hardening rate of the solution-treated specimens.

characterization_methods.key_findings: Al-8: Akv-40 = 294 ± 11 J, one of only three designed alloys with high impact toughness.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Test temperature −40 °C; V-notch perpendicular to the rod axis
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure impact toughness of the solution-treated samples.

analytical_models.equation_role: predict alloy mass density from mass% of C, Al and Mn
analytical_models.model_note: Eq. (3): ρ = 8.10 − 0.102C − 0.10Al − 0.01Mn (g/cm³), with C, Al, Mn in mass%.

computational_details.simulation_method: Empirical analytical model (linear least-squares fit of measured density vs alloy content)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: For Al-8 (Fe30Mn8Al1C: C 0.98, Al 8.08, Mn 30.22 mass%) the model gives ρ ≈ 6.89 g/cm³, matching the measured density of 6.90 g/cm³ (Table 1).

analytical_models.equation_role: σ_TS = σ_UTS (1 + UE): maximum true stress just before necking / crack nucleation
analytical_models.model_note: Eq. (1); σ_UTS is the ultimate tensile strength and UE the uniform elongation.

analytical_models.equation_role: σ_FS = σ_EF / (1 − A): highest local (true) strength during tensile deformation
analytical_models.model_note: Eq. (2); σ_EF is the engineering fracture stress at sample breakage and A the maximum area reduction.

computational_details.simulation_method: Analytical equations converting engineering tensile quantities to true stresses
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: For Al-8, Table 2 lists UTS^a (σ_TS, maximum true stress just before necking) = 1370 MPa and FRS^a (σ_FS, fracture strength) = 2154 MPa.

comparative_performance.note: Al-8 (Fe30Mn8Al1.0C, 294 J) is one of only three of the thirteen designed low-density steels with high impact toughness; the others are Fe30Mn6Al1.0C (354 J) and Fe30Mn10Al1.0C (237 J).

processing_steps.method: high-frequency vacuum induction melting and casting into ingot
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Each steel composition melted in a high-frequency vacuum induction furnace of 50 kg capacity and cast into an ingot of 150 mm diameter.
Ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 5 h prior to hot rolling.

processing_steps.method: hot rolling into rods, followed by air cooling
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Homogenized ingots were hot rolled into rods of 16 mm diameter and air-cooled to room temperature (this is the parent proc_hot-rolled process).
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: rolled from 150 mm diameter ingot into 16 mm diameter rods

processing_steps.method: solution treatment followed by water quenching
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot-rolled rods were solution-treated at 1050 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching; this is the terminal state of the sample used for tensile, Charpy and EBSD/TEM characterization.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Specimens solution-treated at 1050 °C for 2 h + water quenching; two specimens tested and data given as the average value of two specimens.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: standard tensile specimen, gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm, tensile axis parallel to rod axis

fracture_toughness.note: Charpy V-notch impact energy Akv measured at −40 °C (V-notch perpendicular to rod axis); this is impact toughness, not a plane-strain fracture toughness.

strain_hardening_rate.description: Work hardening rate decreases with increasing Al content (Fig. 8(c)); the Al-8 curve is among the lower WH curves of the Al series, with the highest WH rate (~2100 MPa) found for the 6% Al steel.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve of Al-8 after 1050 °C/2 h solution treatment is shown in Fig. 2(c)/figure_001 (Fe30Mn(x)Al1C series); increasing Al raises strength and reduces elongation. The curve is not numerically digitized.

grain_structure.texture: twin boundary fraction f_Tw = 50.3% (fractional twin boundary length, twin boundary length / total boundary length with misorientation >15°)

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed grains intersected by abundant straight, parallel twin boundaries

structures.overall_structure: After solution treatment at 1050 °C for 2 h + water quenching the Fe30Mn8Al1C (Al-8) steel consists of a single-phase FCC austenite (γ); no BCC ferrite and no κ-carbide precipitation are present (SAED shows only γ reflections).

unmapped_findings: Al-8 alloy (Fe30Mn8Al1C) measured chemical composition: C 0.98, Mn 30.22, Al 8.08, Fe Bal. (mass%), with measured density 6.90 g/cm³ (Table 1).
For the Al-8 steel the maximum true stress just before necking (UTS^a, σ_TS) was 1370 MPa and the fracture strength (FRS^a, σ_FS) was 2154 MPa (Table 2).
Across all investigated low-density steels σ_TS and σ_FS were nearly constant at about 1350 MPa and about 2150 MPa, respectively, independent of C, Mn and Al content.

No κ-carbides were observed in the Fe30Mn(x)Al1C steel with 8% Al (Fig. 5(e)); κ-carbide size increases strongly with Al, from ~0.5 nm at 8% Al to ~1 nm at 10% Al, ~1.5 nm at 11% Al and ~15 nm at 12% Al (Table 3 gives D_κ-carbides = 0^a for Al-8).

The κ-carbide strengthening was described by a particle-shear model σ_shear = α f^(1/2) d_Car^(1/2) (Eq. 4); a yield-strength fit R_p0.2 = 478 + 97.1 d_Car^0.5 (slope 97.1 MPa/nm^1/2) was obtained across the designed steels, with flow stress in the absence of κ-carbides of about 478 MPa.

The overall alloy density follows ρ = 8.1 − 0.102C − 0.10Al − 0.01Mn g/cm³ (Eq. 3), differing from previously reported coefficients (0.101 g/cm³ per mass% Al, 0.0085 g/cm³ per mass% Mn, and 0.41 g/cm³ per 1% C).

Engineering stress-strain jumps after yielding in Fig. 2 were caused by removal of the extensometer to allow tests to continue to high plastic strain and do not affect the mechanical property measurements or work hardening rate calculations.
